title: 3D Printing Case for LED Controller
author: Jakub Nedbal
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdici4aw

steps.title: Download CAD and STL files
steps.instruction: Open the KiCAD PCB project, export the 3‑D render as a STEP file, import it into Onshape, and download the two STL files (LEDregulator‑Box Top.stl and LEDregulator‑Box Bottom.stl) from the LED regulator case project page, selecting the printer’s unit (e.g., millimetre) so the files are scaled correctly.

steps.title: 3D print case top and bottom
steps.instruction: Load the downloaded STL files into a Stratasys uPrint SE Plus (or any fused‑deposition‑modelling printer) and print the Top and Bottom case parts following the printer‑manufacturer’s instructions, including any required support structures.

steps.title: Remove support and clean prints
steps.instruction: Dissolve the printed support material by immersing the printed parts in a warm hydrogen‑peroxide bath (observe all local safety regulations and wear appropriate PPE), then rinse the parts thoroughly with copious water and dry them completely before further handling.

steps.title: Tap M3 (or #4‑40) threaded holes
steps.instruction: Using a tap wrench, tap the four blind holes in the Top part with the appropriate thread size: M3 for metric screws or #4‑40 UNC for imperial screws. Perform the tapping in three stages with progressively deeper taps—first the tap marked with one line, then the tap with two lines, and finally the tap with no lines.

steps.title: Assemble PCB into case and fasten
steps.instruction: Slide the assembled PCB into the printed case, place the Bottom part over the PCB, and secure the assembly with four M3 × 10 mm countersunk screws (or four #4‑40 UNC 3/8‑inch countersunk screws where imperial threads are preferred) using a screwdriver or Allen key as appropriate.
